title: Mapping-space pushout for three directed quasicategorical faces
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, faces, quasicategories and right mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], coherent rigidification $\mathfrak C$ and its simplicial mapping sets of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], and derived enriched coends in chronological order from [lem-coef-derived-space-module-coyoneda]. Let $K\to H=\Lambda^3_2$ be a simplicial map. For every nonempty face $J$ in $H$, put $K_J=K\times_H\Delta^J$ and assume $K_J$ is a quasicategory. Write $A_i=\mathfrak C[K_{\{i\}}]$. For $i<j$, write $M_{ij}(u,v)=\mathfrak C[K_{\{i,j\}}](u,v)$, a simplicial bimodule on $A_i^{\mathrm{op}}\times A_j$ by enriched composition. For $x\in K_0$, $z\in K_3$, define the following homotopy types of spaces:
$$P(x,z)=M_{01}(x,-)\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbb L}M_{13}(-,z),$$
$$R(x,z)=M_{01}(x,-)\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbb L}M_{12}\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbb L}M_{23}(-,z),$$
$$D(x,z)=M_{03}(x,z).$$
All composition maps here are maps in the homotopy theory of enriched modules: compose in the indicated triangle face and invert its full-edge mapping comparison, supplied by [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]. They do not require a strict retraction from a triangle face to an edge face. Composition in the face $K_{123}$ gives $R\to P$. Composition first in $K_{012}$ and then in $K_{023}$ gives $R\to D$. These maps, together with composition in $\mathfrak C[K]$, induce a natural equivalence of homotopy types
$$P(x,z)\amalg^h_{R(x,z)}D(x,z)\simeq\mathfrak C[K](x,z).$$
Here the left side is a homotopy pushout of spaces, not an ordinary pushout of component sets; under this equivalence its map from $D$ is induced by the actual inclusion $K_{03}\hookrightarrow K$. For vertices $u\in K_i$, $v\in K_j$ with $i\leq j$ and $(i,j)\ne(0,3)$, the actual inclusion of any face $F\subseteq H$ containing $i,j$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\mathfrak C[K_F](u,v)\longrightarrow\mathfrak C[K](u,v).$$
All these comparisons are natural for simplicial maps over $H$. No cocartesian lifts, categorical enlargement of $K$, or face equivalence after such an enlargement is assumed or concluded.

source.place: Supporting the inherited operadic extension branch of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, paragraph 2 (coherent middle adjunction): directed gluing of the faces 012, 123, 023 in the face comparison required by HA 3.1.2.4 Agent-formulated auxiliary statement, not a quoted numbered theorem of HTT; archival source WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched homotopy-theoretic assertion.

proof.text: For any face $F$ containing $i\leq j$, right-pinched mapping simplices from $u\in K_i$ to $v\in K_j$ in $K_F$ lie in $K_{ij}$: their image in $H$ has initial vertices all $i$ and final vertex $j$, so every simplex of that image uses only $i,j$. Thus $\operatorname{Map}^R_{K_{ij}}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Map}^R_{K_F}(u,v)$ is an isomorphism, including $i=j$ with $K_{ii}=K_i$. The natural $p$ and $\theta$ equivalences of [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution] identify the actual edge inclusion on rigidification mapping sets with this isomorphism. Two-out-of-three makes it a weak equivalence. These are enriched composition-compatible comparisons because they are induced by inclusions. In particular all inclusions from a vertex fibre or edge into a triangle are homotopically full on their own vertices. No retraction is used.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; full edge and vertex comparisons inside a quasicategorical face. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.

proof.text: All labels of a rigidification path are nondecreasing: in each generating simplex the arrows go from an earlier to a later vertex, and composing cannot reverse this. Mapping sets in decreasing label direction are therefore empty. Put $U=K_{012}\cup K_{123}$ and $W=K_{02}\cup K_{23}$. Degreewise, $K_{012}\cap K_{123}=K_{12}$, $K_{02}\cap K_{23}=K_2$, and $U\cap K_{023}=W$; the three triangles cover $K$. These are equalities of inverse images of faces in $H$, so each displayed union is a simplicial-set pushout. The left adjoint $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] preserves these pushouts, makes every piece cofibrant and every inclusion a cofibration. These strict pushouts compute homotopy pushouts: take a cofibrant replacement of each span as supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping], with cofibrant objects and cofibration legs, and compare it to the original cofibrant span using clause (b) of [lem-coef-model-cofibrant-colimit-comparison]. Thus the three gluings below have their actual inclusion cocones.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; decompose the three-face union into directed pushouts. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.

proof.text: We will change an indexing category along identity-on-objects local weak equivalences. The Quillen equivalence $v_!\dashv v^*$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus], applied to Kan-model simplicial sets and to the opposite indexing categories, justifies this for left and right modules. Indeed the quotient defining coends gives $(v_!X)\otimes_B Y=X\otimes_A v^*Y$: both sides impose exactly the same action relations. Apply this identity to cofibrant replacements and the derived unit/counit equivalences. It identifies the derived coends after changing the base and restricting the modules, compatibly with every action map. The objectwise invariance and Fubini assertions of [lem-coef-derived-space-module-coyoneda] allow the endpoint mapping modules to be replaced by the actual edge modules from step 1. This calculation retains any outer module variables; it changes indexing, without choosing a strict inverse functor to any face inclusion.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; change of indexing for the bar calculations. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-directed-enriched-amalgamation] to $\mathfrak C[K_{012}]\leftarrow\mathfrak C[K_{12}]\to\mathfrak C[K_{123}]$, with blocks $L=K_0$, $O=K_1\amalg K_2$, $R=K_3$. Step 1 verifies both homotopically full overlap hypotheses and step 2 verifies absence of backward arrows. Thus all mapping sets of either triangle map by weak equivalences into $\mathfrak C[U]$, and
$$\mathfrak C[U](x,z)\simeq X\otimes_B^{\mathbb L}Y,$$
where $B=\mathfrak C[K_{12}]$, $X=\mathfrak C[K_{012}](x,-)|_B$ and $Y=\mathfrak C[K_{123}](-,z)|_B$. In particular the endpoint actions are the actual triangle compositions.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; first gluing of 012 and 123 along 12. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.

proof.text:
The category $B$ has two blocks $K_1,K_2$ and no backward arrows. Apply [lem-coef-triangular-bar-excision] to these $X,Y$. After the base and module comparisons of steps 1 and 3, its two outside terms are
$$P=M_{01}(x,-)\otimes_{A_1}^{\mathbb L}M_{13}(-,z),\qquad Q=M_{02}(x,-)\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbb L}M_{23}(-,z),$$
and its mixed term is $R$ from the statement. Therefore $\mathfrak C[U](x,z)\simeq P\amalg_R^h Q$. The arrow $R\to P$ acts on $Y$ and is composition in $K_{123}$; $R\to Q$ acts on $X$ and is composition in $K_{012}$. The excision theorem specifies these maps as well as the comparison, so this identifies the cocone and not just its objects.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; two-block bar excision for 12. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-directed-enriched-amalgamation] again to $\mathfrak C[K_{02}]\leftarrow A_2\to\mathfrak C[K_{23}]$. Its three blocks are $K_0,K_2,K_3$; step 1 verifies homotopically full vertex overlaps. This gives $\mathfrak C[W](x,z)\simeq Q$ after step 3, and weak equivalences from the two edge mapping sets on all other pairs. Under the map $W\hookrightarrow U$, this comparison is the map from $Q$ in step 5: both are the derived composition of the same inclusions of 02 and 23. Under $W\hookrightarrow K_{023}$ it is composition in 023 followed by the full-edge comparison identifying that face's extreme mapping module with $D=M_{03}$. The naturality and augmentation compatibility in the amalgamation and coend theorems give these identifications in the homotopy theory of modules.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; compute the attachment intersection 02 union 23 and both maps. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.

proof.text:
Now set $T=\mathfrak C[W]$, $V=\mathfrak C[K_{023}]$, $B'=\mathfrak C[U]$, and use $I=\{0<1<2<3\}$, $S=\{0,2,3\}$ in [lem-coef-extreme-bimodule-attachment]. Step 6 and the full-edge comparisons of step 1 show $T\to V$ is a weak equivalence on every mapping set except possibly $K_0\times K_3$. The map $T\to B'$ is a weak equivalence on both endpoint blocks, by steps 4 and 6 and their shared vertex-fibre comparisons. Decreasing-label mapping sets are empty by step 2, and the object functions are exactly the prescribed inclusions. The homotopy pushout is $\mathfrak C[K]$, with its actual face inclusions, by step 2. Consequently
$$\mathfrak C[K](x,z)\simeq (P\amalg_R^h Q)\amalg_Q^h D.$$
The same attachment theorem makes $\mathfrak C[U]\to\mathfrak C[K]$ a weak equivalence on every other mapping set.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; attach the remaining face 023 only at the extreme mapping block. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.

proof.text: Pasting the two pushouts gives $(P\amalg_R^h Q)\amalg_Q^h D\simeq P\amalg_R^h D$. To see the map, a cocone to any space $Z$ consists of maps from $P,Q,D$, a homotopy on $R$, and a homotopy equating the map from $Q$ to the restriction of the one from $D$. Eliminating the $Q$ map and this specified homotopy leaves exactly maps $P,D\to Z$ agreeing coherently on $R$ through $R\to Q\to D$. This is the pushout universal property, including its higher data. By steps 5 and 6 this composite acts first in 012 and then in 023. The map from $D$ is the actual 03 inclusion, since throughout its comparison is inverse to the actual edge-to-023 mapping equivalence and the final cocone uses 023 inclusion.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; pushout pasting and identification of the actual extreme-edge map. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.

proof.text: For a pair other than $(0,3)$, some triangle of $U$ contains its labels: 012 contains all pairs without 3, and 123 contains all pairs without 0. Its actual map into $\mathfrak C[U]$ is a weak equivalence by step 4, and into $\mathfrak C[K]$ by step 7. The edge-to-triangle comparison of step 1 therefore makes the actual $K_{ij}\to K$ comparison a weak equivalence. For any face $F$ containing the pair, step 1 and the factorization $K_{ij}\to K_F\to K$ give the result by two-out-of-three, also for $i=j$. Every decomposition is by inverse images of the fixed labelled faces; every bar, composition pairing, coend comparison and gluing comparison above is natural in such maps. The full construction is therefore natural for all simplicial maps over $H$, without any choice of cocartesian edges or enlargement.

source.place: Agent argument, using Appendix A.3 background; all remaining actual face maps and naturality. The three directed bar/attachment inputs are separately stated nodes, not asserted to be numbered theorems of HTT.
